title: 2026-10-22_The_Supreme_Backdoor_Factory_Investigation_4e9
description: Investigate and respond to the threat posed by The Supreme Backdoor Factory malware in our network environment.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Supreme Backdoor Factory is a set of malicious GitHub repositories used to deliver payloads. It involves creating scheduled tasks to download and execute PowerShell code from various URLs. Your task is to investigate and respond to this threat in our network environment.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the target host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: target
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the following credentials to access the target host:
- Hostname: target
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Activity
levels.content: While monitoring network traffic, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate this activity and identify any suspicious services or processes that might be responsible. Submit the systemd timer name responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution: Check running services and network connections. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services. The suspicious service is the one responsible for the unusual outbound connections. The final flag is lab-checkin.timer.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and network connections.

levels.title: Analyze Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Now that you've identified the suspicious service, determine how it maintains persistence on the system. Find out how this service is automatically started after system reboots. Submit the systemd timer name responsible for the service's persistence.
levels.solution: Investigate systemd services and timers. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers. The systemd timer responsible for the service's persistence is the one that starts the service automatically. The final flag is lab-checkin.timer.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Examine if the suspicious activity on the target host has led to any lateral movement within the network. Check for any file transfers or remote execution attempts to other hosts. Submit the systemd service name responsible for lateral movement.
levels.solution: Review system logs and scheduled tasks. Use the command `journalctl -xe` to review system logs. The script or service responsible for lateral movement is the one that performs file transfers or remote execution. The final flag is payload-transfer.service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Review system logs and scheduled tasks.
